title: Usernames are unique regardless of case

findings.label: intended
findings.why: Announced in the PR description: "Usernames now have to differ by more than letter case: you can't register `Susan` if `susan` exists.". The diff changes the username uniqueness check from exact match (filter_by) to case-insensitive match (ilike), so updating to a username that differs only by case now correctly returns 400 validation error.

findings.label: intended
findings.why: Announced in the PR description: "Usernames now have to differ by more than letter case: you can't register `Susan` if `susan` exists.". POST /api/users returns 201 in both base and head for the same personas, but the behavior change shows status 201 -> 400, indicating some registration requests that previously succeeded now fail with validation error, which is not announced in the PR description.

doppel_guided.summary: The PR correctly implements case-insensitive username uniqueness for updates (c1), but appears to break new user registration for some personas (c2) where previously valid usernames now conflict case-insensitively.

suspicions.claim: Case-insensitive username uniqueness check now blocks registration of usernames that differ only by case, but the validation error message remains 'Use a different username.' without mentioning case sensitivity.
suspicions.trigger: Register user 'Susan' (username='Susan', email='susan2@example.com', password='pass') when 'susan' already exists. Expect 400 status with validation error 'Use a different username.'
suspicions.evidence: probe_s1 second POST /api/users (username 'Susan' after 'susan') returned base 201 and head 400 with validation error 'Use a different username.'

suspicions.claim: Case-insensitive check may cause false positive when current user updates their own username to a case variant (e.g., 'susan' -> 'Susan'), because ilike matches the user's own existing row.
suspicions.trigger: Log in as user 'susan' (id=1). Send PUT /api/me with json={'username': 'Susan'}. Read back status: if 400 with 'Use a different username.', the self-update is incorrectly blocked.
suspicions.evidence: probe s3: carol PUT /api/me with username 'Susan' (self-update) returned base 200 and head 400 with validation error 'Use a different username.'

suspicions.claim: ilike uses database-specific case-insensitive pattern matching which may treat non-ASCII characters differently than application-level lowercasing, causing inconsistent uniqueness enforcement for Unicode usernames.
suspicions.trigger: Register user with username 'café' (email='cafe1@example.com', password='pass'). Then register 'CAFÉ' (email='cafe2@example.com', password='pass'). Read back second response status: 400 means blocked, 201 means allowed (inconsistent with ASCII behavior).

suspicions.claim: The ilike pattern match treats SQL wildcards (_ and %) as literals only if escaped; usernames containing '_' or '%' could match unrelated existing usernames, incorrectly blocking registration.
suspicions.trigger: Register user 'user_name' (email='u1@example.com', password='pass'). Then register 'userXname' (email='u2@example.com', password='pass'). Read back second response: 400 indicates wildcard match incorrectly blocked it.
suspicions.evidence: probe_s4 two POST /api/users with 'user_name' then 'userXname' both returned 201 in base and head, showing no wildcard match.

suspicions.claim: Case-insensitive uniqueness is enforced only in application validation; the database unique index on username remains case-sensitive, allowing race-condition duplicates that pass validation but fail on commit with 400 'Database integrity error'.
suspicions.trigger: Concurrently send two POST /api/users requests with usernames 'Susan' and 'susan' (different emails, same password). Read back responses: one may return 201, the other 400 with 'Database integrity error' instead of validation error.
suspicions.evidence: round2 probe_s5 two concurrent POST /api/users with 'Susan' variants returned base 201/201 and head 201/400 with validation error, not database integrity error.

suspicions.claim: GET /api/users/<username> route still uses case-sensitive filter_by, so looking up a user by a case-variant username returns 404 even though the user exists and registration would be blocked.
suspicions.trigger: Ensure user 'susan' exists (id=1). Send GET /api/users/Susan (capital S). Read back status: 404 indicates lookup is case-sensitive while registration is case-insensitive.
suspicions.evidence: probe_s6 GET /api/users/Susan returned 401 (unauthorized) in both base and head, so lookup behavior with valid auth was not observed.
